name: GGUF Q8_0 (legacy block-8 symmetric)
quality_delta: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (quant-gguf-kquant-study): WikiText-2 ppl 7.33 vs 7.32 F16 (+0.01); unweighted mean 69.41 vs 69.47 (-0.09% AvgLoss); size 8138 MiB (-46.87%). This is the reference-ish GGUF baseline: 8.5008 bpw includes block scales, so it is genuinely close to lossless.
notes: The practical near-lossless GGUF point and the format llama.cpp still recommends for multimodal projectors, for --leave-output-tensor, and for any tensor you do not want degraded (its quantize README advises keeping mmproj in bf16 or q8_0 because projector quality directly affects generation). Weight-only: activations stay in FP16/BF16 at runtime, so there is no '4-bit activations with hardware support' claim to make here. ggml has bespoke dequantize+gemm kernels per type, but no accelerator has a GGUF/k-quant path in silicon; everything is dequantized on the fly. vLLM explicitly labels its GGUF support experimental and under-optimized and positions it as a memory-footprint tool (quant-vllm-gguf-doc). Q8_0 is also the activation format ggml uses internally: quantized k-quant GEMMs quantize the activation to Q8_0 inside the kernel (quant-gguf-kquant-study). That is the one place a GGUF type touches a matrix multiply with a non-fp16 operand, and it is still a software-side requantization, not an INT8 hardware path.
